text:
If you can steal an hour outside, make it this afternoon. Clouds should break for a mostly sunny finish, with a chilly high right around 53 and the north wind easing as the day goes on. The lake will follow suit, with waves settling to a foot or less by afternoon, so today is your better waterfront window. Tonight stays quiet through the evening, then rain showers become likely after 1am, with a low near 40.

Friday is the turn. Rain arrives early and hangs around, with a high near 62, but the bigger issue is wind. The forecasters have raised the gust concern for Burlington, and south winds could gust close to 40 mph. On the lake, winds may reach 30 knots with waves building as high as 6 feet. Keep boats and loose patio gear secured tonight, and plan indoor Friday activities, or be off the water before the rain and wind build.

week.blurb: Sunny and cool, near 53, then rain arrives after 1am; plan daytime outdoors, but keep the morning commute flexible.
A soaking, windy Friday, near 62, with rain likely all day and gusts nearing 39; keep plans indoors.
Blustery and chilly, near 43, with a stray early shower or flurry; the European model hints warmer, but I’d dress for cold.
Sunshine returns Sunday, near 54, with light south winds and a clear, comfortable setup for outdoor plans.
A sunny, mild Monday near 59, with south winds and an easy day for errands, walks, or yard work.
Mostly sunny and mild Tuesday, near 60, with light winds and no weather complication for outdoor plans.
Mostly sunny Wednesday, near 56, with a light breeze and a cool, quiet finish to the day.
